tr.td: Cognitive evaluation for progressive memory loss: history from patient and caregiver, MoCA, function, mood, safety, and reversible-cause tests
Four-week follow-up: results and MRI review, diagnosis disclosure, and behavioral neurology consultation
Three-month dementia review: donepezil, safety plan, caregiver burden, and advance care planning
Same-day sick visit for a head cold with night-time confusion
Reversible-cause tests (blood count, metabolic panel, vitamin B12, folate, TSH) and one non-contrast brain MRI; syphilis and HIV testing only with risk factors or atypical features
Behavioral neurology consultation to confirm the diagnosis, consider the type and biomarker testing, and advise on treatment and driving

Donepezil trial, 5 mg daily for four to eight weeks then 10 mg, with heart rate, fainting, gastrointestinal effects, weight, and sleep checked at each visit; avoid anticholinergic drugs, first-generation antihistamines, benzodiazepines, and sleeping pills (AGS Beers Criteria)
Safety: stop driving at CDR 1, keep the home free of firearms, medical identification for wandering, supervised medicines and finances, and home safety
Caregiver support: Zarit Burden Interview at diagnosis and every six to twelve months, education, adult day program and respite, and Alzheimer's Association support services

Monitor on the CMID dementia schedule: medication review and neuropsychiatric screen at every visit; MoCA, ADL and IADL, CDR or FAST stage, depression screen, fall risk, driving, and advance care planning yearly; repeat tests or imaging only with a sudden change
Advance care planning while he can take part: name a health care agent and record his values and wishes
Complete the reversible-cause tests and brain MRI and discuss the diagnosis with him and his caregiver by the four-week visit
Tests and MRI showed no reversible cause; diagnosis of mild dementia of undetermined type discussed with both
A safety plan in place by the three-month review: no driving, medicines supervised, finances overseen, and medical identification worn
Stopped driving after the consultation; caregiver gives medicines from a weekly organizer and oversees bill paying with his agreement; medical identification bracelet worn
Donepezil at 10 mg daily without side effects and with resting heart rate 55 or above by the six-month review
On 10 mg for three months; heart rate 60; no nausea, diarrhea, weight loss, or vivid dreams
Caregiver burden assessed and support in place by the six-month review
Zarit Burden Interview 24 at three months; caregiver education program completed and two days a week of adult day program begun
Name a health care agent and record his values and wishes while he can take full part, by the three-month review
Health care agent named and his wishes recorded at the three-month review
